key_concept: Each biomolecule is matched to its function: starch stores energy, antibodies fight infection, concanavalin A is a lectin, and GLUT-4 transports glucose (NCERT table of protein functions).
steps: A. Starch is a plant storage polysaccharide made of glucose units, so it serves as energy storage. A matches II.
B. Antibodies are immunoglobulins made by B-cells (plasma cells). They bind antigens and fight infection. B matches I.
C. Concanavalin A is a lectin, a carbohydrate-binding protein obtained from the jack bean. C matches IV.
D. GLUT-4 is a membrane protein that carries glucose into cells. It is insulin-regulated and found in muscle and adipose tissue. D matches III.
The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III, which is option (2).
why_not_others: Option (3) swaps C and D, wrongly calling concanavalin A a glucose transporter and GLUT-4 a lectin. Options (1) and (4) also wrongly assign starch to fighting infection and antibody to energy storage.
common_trap: Students know that concanavalin A binds sugars and so confuse it with glucose transport, picking option (3).
time_saving_tip: Starch = energy storage (A-II) at once leaves only options (2) and (3). Then recall that the name GLUT-4 itself signals 'glucose transporter' (D-III), which gives option (2).
